calculator.q1: How do I use the scientific calculator?
calculator.a1: Type a sum or tap the keys, for example 2 × (3 + 4) or sin(30). The result shows as you type; press = or Enter to keep it in the history.
calculator.a2: The DEG/RAD button switches the angle unit for sin, cos, tan and their inverses. It starts in degrees, so sin(30) is 0.5.
calculator.q3: In what order does it calculate?
calculator.a3: Brackets first, then powers and factorials, then × and ÷, then + and −. −2^2 is −4, and 2π or 3(4 + 1) multiply without a × sign.
calculator.a4: % divides by 100: 50% is 0.5 and 200 × 15% is 30. Ans stands for the last result, so you can carry on from it.
calculator.a5: The last 20 sums are kept in this browser only, so they are there next time. Clear history removes them. Nothing is sent anywhere.

notepad.a1: In this browser's local storage, on your device. It is saved a moment after you stop typing and is there when you come back. It is never uploaded.
notepad.q2: Can I open the note on another device?
notepad.a2: No, the note stays in this browser. Download it as a .txt file, or copy it, to move it. Clearing your browsing data deletes the note.
notepad.a3: Once the page has loaded, typing and saving work without a connection, because nothing goes to a server.
notepad.q4: Can I open a text file?
notepad.a4: Yes. Open reads a .txt, .md, .csv or similar file into the notepad on your device. It replaces the note; Undo brings the old one back for a few seconds.
notepad.q5: What if I have it open in two tabs?
notepad.a5: A tab you are not typing in picks up what the other tab saved. Private windows may not keep the note after they are closed.

markdown.a1: Headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, links, images, lists, task lists, quotes, code spans and fenced code blocks, horizontal rules and GitHub-style tables.
markdown.q2: How do I convert Markdown to HTML?
markdown.a2: Paste your Markdown and press Copy HTML, or Download HTML for a complete page. The HTML is clean, with no classes or scripts added.
markdown.a3: No. Raw HTML tags are shown as text, and only web, email, phone and relative links are linked, so a pasted document cannot run scripts.
markdown.q4: Is my text saved or uploaded?
markdown.a4: Your text stays in this browser and is kept for your next visit. It is never uploaded. Images in the preview load from the addresses you write.
markdown.q5: How do I make a table?
markdown.a5: Write a header row with | between cells, then a row of dashes like |---|---|, then one line per row. Colons in the dash row set alignment: :--- left, :---: centre, ---: right.

gradient.q1: How do I make a CSS gradient?
gradient.a1: Pick a type (linear, radial or conic), set the colours and their positions, and adjust the angle or shape. The CSS updates as you go; press Copy CSS.
gradient.a2: A colour at a position along the gradient, from 0% to 100%. Add up to six stops; the gradient blends between them in order of position.
gradient.q3: Why are there two background lines?
gradient.a3: The first line is a solid colour for very old browsers; the second is the gradient. Every current browser uses the gradient.
gradient.q4: Can I save the gradient as an image?
gradient.a4: Yes. Choose a size (desktop, phone, 1440p or square) and press Save PNG. It is drawn in your browser.
gradient.a5: Linear blends along a line at an angle (90° is left to right). Radial spreads from the centre as a circle or ellipse. Conic sweeps around the centre like a colour wheel.

fancy-text.q1: How does the fancy text generator work?
fancy-text.a1: It swaps letters and numbers for look-alike Unicode characters, such as mathematical bold or circled letters. They are text, not images, so they paste anywhere.
fancy-text.q2: Where can I use these fonts?
fancy-text.a2: Instagram and TikTok bios, X posts, Discord, WhatsApp, YouTube comments and game names. Some apps or fonts may show a box for a character they lack.
fancy-text.q3: Why are some letters not changed?
fancy-text.a3: Unicode has these styles only for A–Z, a–z and some digits. Other letters, accents and Chinese, Japanese or Korean text stay as you typed them.
fancy-text.a4: Screen readers may read them letter by letter or skip them, and search does not match them. Use them for decoration, not for important text.
fancy-text.q5: How do I copy a style?
fancy-text.a5: Type your text, then press Copy next to the style you like. Upside-down text is also reversed, so it reads correctly turned over.
